title: Other inventory movements
log: 2026-11-01T08:04:31Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The bank point covers holding costs and FIFO/LIFO valuation, while the new point is about returns, drawings and advertising stock movements changing the inventory card, which is a different idea.

draft.title: Other inventory movements
card: Inventory is not only bought and sold. Some other events also change the units and value on the inventory card.
Goods sent back to a supplier reduce inventory. Goods a customer sends back to the business increase inventory, if they can be resold.
When the owner takes goods for personal use, inventory falls. This is not a sale, and the owner is not paid by customers.
Stock given away or used for advertising leaves inventory, even though no sale is made.
draft.remember: If goods leave or return to the shelves, the inventory card changes, even with no sale.

a.q: Tam owns a bike shop in Ballarat. She takes a helmet from stock for her son. What happens to the inventory card?
opts: Inventory falls because a sale was made
a.why: Goods taken by the owner for private use leave inventory, so the card shows one less helmet. It is not a sale, so the last option is wrong, even though stock has gone.
a.clue: Did the helmet stay in the shop?

b.q: Noor runs a gift shop in Geelong. She returns 4 faulty mugs to her supplier. A customer also returns 2 resaleable mugs for a refund. What is the net change in mugs on the inventory card?
b.why: Returning 4 mugs to the supplier cuts inventory by 4. The 2 resaleable mugs from the customer add 2 back. The net change is a fall of 2. Falling by 6 wrongly treats both returns as leaving stock.
b.clue: One return takes stock out and the other brings stock in.
